row.scim_price_text: Free to sign up; pay per ride and meal
row.team_price_text: Free to sign up; pay per ride and meal
row.evidence: Uber's pricing page says "Uber for Business is free to signup" with no paid tiers, and the SCIM onboarding guide asks only that you "be onboarded to a Uber for Business organization and have admin access to it".
row.notes: No plans or seats: organisations pay for rides and meals, and the pricing footnote says use via API or integration partners may incur additional fees, which may cover SCIM. SCIM 2.0 has pre-built Okta, OneLogin and Entra apps; other IdPs need the account manager to assign SCIM scopes, and Okta provisioning must be activated by Uber support. SCIM creates an employee record and emails an invitation to link the person's own Uber account; deprovisioning unlinks it. SAML SSO is a separate onboarding done with Uber support, and no plan or price is published for it, so sso_plan is null. The SCIM and Employees API pages are public on developer.uber.com but are rendered client-side, so quotes are cited from the docs JS bundle, with page_url pointing to each page. Also offers SFTP CSV employee sync.

plans.name: Uber for Business
plans.price_text: Free to sign up; pay for rides and meals (pay per trip or monthly bill)
plans.notes: Single platform with no paid tiers; API or integration-partner use may incur additional fees (c2).

auth.token_source: OAuth 2.0 via auth.uber.com; IdP apps authenticate with a U4B admin account (no service accounts); custom apps use a developer.uber.com app with SCIM scopes assigned by the account manager
auth.notes: The SCIM authentication guide says application tokens are needed again every 30 days and cannot be refreshed; the Okta and OneLogin apps use an authorisation-code flow tied to an admin account, whose expiry is not stated.

operations.notes: Groups support POST, PATCH, GET, DELETE and list (no PUT).

deprovision.data_retained: The employee's personal Uber account remains; only the link to the business organization is removed. OneLogin suspend keeps the account so it can be restored.
deprovision.notes: No seat pricing, so frees_seat does not apply.

filtering.notes: From the Entra gallery mapping (userName supported for filtering).

attributes.notes: userName maps to the user's email; only mobile numbers with country code are supported.

roles.notes: Groups map to Uber for Business groups (policy groups); users with no group land in the General group. No admin-role mapping documented.

limitations.text: SCIM does not create an Uber account; it creates an employee record and emails an invitation to link the employee's own Uber account.
No service accounts: SCIM authenticates as a U4B admin account.
Create-group requests cannot include members; patch-group is limited to 100 members per request.
Okta provisioning has to be activated by Uber support.

scim.notes: Any Uber for Business organization admin can set up SCIM; the platform has no paid tiers. Okta provisioning needs Uber support to activate it, and other IdPs need the account manager to assign SCIM scopes. SSO onboarding is a separate process and is not required.

auth.notes: Scope name read from the endpoint reference pages in the docs bundle.

endpoints.purpose: Get an employee of an organization
Get a paginated list of employees
Delete a group of an organization

user_api.notes: Employees API (scope business.employees). The pricing page footnote says use via API or integration partners may incur additional fees, so whether it costs extra is unclear.

okta.notes: Uber for Business app (provisioning). A separate older "Uber" Okta app is SSO only.

onelogin.notes: From Uber's own OneLogin guide; OneLogin catalogue page not loaded.

fallbacks.other_sync: SFTP CSV employee roster sync (add, remove, replace)
